headline: High: ctx can read/write shared filesystem and browser/API surfaces while Botpress may ingest untrusted content, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, and ctx can observe Claude Code events plus filesystem content. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where ctx outputs or files could be treated as instructions by Botpress. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Botpress consumes ctx-produced files or messages as trusted instructions
IF ctx writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace or log that Botpress later parses
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic instruction parsing of shared files
Add provenance tags to ctx outputs
Review any shared clipboard or message queue paths
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx explicitly touches agent entities, MCP servers, harness records, graph data, and runtime logs, and it can access filesystem and external APIs. Botpress has no stated data-class restrictions and no network egress, but it can still receive or expose data through its support workflows. A shared workspace or log path could leak ctx-managed sensitive records into Botpress outputs.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or log directory
IF Botpress is configured to surface ctx-managed records in responses or tickets
mitigations: Store sensitive ctx logs outside Botpress reach
Redact graph and audit data before handoff
Use separate OS principals
Audit shared mounts and environment variables
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention at the boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can install packages, and ctx also writes to filesystem and runs browsers while supporting multiple instances. Botpress lacks a concurrency model, so overlapping writes or package changes in a shared environment can conflict even without explicit git state. The pairwise overlap is real enough for medium severity, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF package installation targets the same environment or lockfile
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments
Pin dependencies and lockfiles
Serialize package-install steps
Mount read-only shared inputs
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a harness/knowledge-graph agent that observes tool events and logs, so its outputs are likely to be treated as structured context. Botpress is a customer-support agent, which commonly turns upstream context into user-facing actions. Without a documented verification step, A-to-B handoff can propagate errors into responses or operational decisions, making the default path dangerous.
conditions: IF Botpress uses ctx output as authoritative context without a verification step
IF ctx-derived facts are rendered directly into customer-facing replies or automations
mitigations: Require human review for high-impact outputs
Add a verification checklist before Botpress acts
Mark ctx outputs as untrusted by default
Compare ctx claims against source records
requires-engineering: implement confidence-gated routing

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly handles audit/runtime logs, harness records, and graph data, which can carry regulated or retention-sensitive content. Botpress has no documented residency, retention, or certification controls in the profile. Because the compliance posture is undocumented on both sides, the safest reading is a retention/logging mismatch risk rather than a proven residency breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx logs or graph data
IF Botpress retains or republishes that data under a different policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Minimize retention in both systems
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
Review vendor policy docs before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-aware retention controls
